Class TrainingDriver

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.training.TrainingDriver
public final class TrainingDriver extends Object
Launches an application once for a training run and takes it down again, whatever happens in between.

One run is: launch the archive with java -jar, wait until the application is ready, send it the workload, call back, stop it. Every phase has a timeout, all of the application's output goes to a file, and every process the run started is gone when run(Path, Path, List, TrainingSettings, Path, Path, TrainingDriver.AfterWorkload, BuildLogger) returns or throws, the application's own children included. A build JVM that exits or is stopped in an orderly way while a run is in progress, such as by SIGTERM on Linux and macOS, takes the application down with it through a shutdown hook. One that is killed outright runs no hook and leaves the application running: after SIGKILL, or when Windows terminates it.

The driver names no build tool and knows nothing about what the run is for: the caller passes the JVM arguments that make it a recording or a cache training, and reads the result in its TrainingDriver.AfterWorkload callback.

  • Method Details

    • run

      public static TrainingDriver.Outcome run(Path java, Path jar, List<String> jvmArguments, TrainingSettings settings, Path workingDirectory, Path logFile, TrainingDriver.AfterWorkload afterWorkload, BuildLogger log) throws IOException, InterruptedException
      Runs the application once.

      The command is <java> <settings.jvmArgs> <jvmArguments> -jar <jar>, so the caller's arguments win over the user's. The application runs in workingDirectory with its standard input closed and its output appended to logFile. Its environment is the build's, without the ambient JVM option variables, plus TrainingSettings.environment() and a free loopback port in TrainingSettings.portVariable().

      The exit status is reported, not judged: a caller that needs an orderly exit asks TrainingDriver.Outcome.requireOrderlyExit().

      Parameters:
      java - the java executable to launch with
      jar - the archive to launch; with a layout, its application jar
      jvmArguments - the caller's JVM arguments, placed after the user's
      settings - how to reach, exercise and stop the application
      workingDirectory - the application's working directory, created if it does not exist
      logFile - the file the application's output is appended to
      afterWorkload - what to do between the workload and the stop
      log - where the phases are reported
      Returns:
      how the run ended
      Throws:
      IOException - if a phase fails or times out; the message names the phase, the time since the launch and the log, and quotes the end of the log
      InterruptedException - if the thread is interrupted; every process has been reaped by then
